sources.title: Introducing Mercury Edit 2
sources.evidence: Exact-model launch identifies Mercury Edit 2 as an Inception diffusion LLM for next-edit prediction, generating tokens in parallel. It describes edit-data training and KTO preference alignment, and announces API availability. No parameter count or denoiser backbone is specified.

sources.title: Inception Blog: Mercury Edit 2 launch index
sources.evidence: Official blog index dates Introducing Mercury Edit 2 to March 30, 2026; paired with the announcement of immediate availability, this establishes the public release date.

sources.title: Models - Inception Platform
sources.evidence: Exact Mercury Edit 2 row specifies text, FIM and edit endpoints, 32K context for each, and 8,192 maximum output tokens. The model description identifies code editing, autocomplete and next-edit suggestions. These limits conflict with live model-list metadata.

sources.title: Terms of Use - Inception
sources.evidence: Service terms reserve ownership of the services to Inception, provide restricted non-transferable service/content usage rights and prohibit reverse engineering. Together with the exact-model hosted API release, this supports proprietary service licensing, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: Inception API OpenAPI specification
sources.evidence: Directly fetched public JSON. FIMCompletionRequest and EditCompletionRequest fully enumerate request fields with no reasoning control; both cap max_tokens at 8192. Endpoint descriptions explicitly exclude tool calls. Model-list examples instead specify 128000 context and 32000 output for mercury-edit-2.

sources.title: Reasoning Efforts - Inception Platform
sources.evidence: Reasoning-effort controls apply to mercury-3, mercury-2.5 and mercury-2 on chat completions. Mercury Edit 2 uses only the separately documented FIM/edit endpoints, whose exhaustive request schemas expose no reasoning mode.

sources.title: Live Inception FIM model listing
sources.evidence: Unauthenticated read-only GET at 2026-10-26T20:54:59.463946Z returned id mercury-edit-2, context_length 128000, max_output_length 32000, text input/output, supported_features [], and endpoints edit.completions/fim.completions. The created field is 1743465660 (2025-04-01), predating the official launch; it is not used as release evidence.

sources.title: Live Inception Edit model listing
sources.evidence: Unauthenticated read-only GET at 2026-10-26T20:54:59.665860Z returned exact id mercury-edit-2 with context_length 128000 and max_output_length 32000, matching the FIM listing but contradicting the 32K/8192 documentation. Its created timestamp 1743465660 is retained as conflicting metadata, not public-release evidence.

sources.title: Research - Inception
sources.evidence: Inspected the first-party research index for later architecture or count disclosures. The listed Mercury technical report is from June 17, 2025; no Mercury Edit 2-specific report or comparison table was found in this index.

sources.title: Mercury: Ultra-Fast Language Models Based on Diffusion
sources.evidence: June 2025 first-party report describes Mercury Coder Mini and Small and their Transformer-based denoisers. It contains no Mercury Edit 2 reference; neither its backbone description nor any sibling specification is transferred to the March 2026 edit model.

sources.title: Introducing Mercury 2.5
sources.evidence: Later first-party model comparison discusses Mercury 2.5 versus Mercury 2 and describes the former as the largest diffusion language model then trained. It contains no exact Mercury Edit 2 count or backbone disclosure.

sources.title: Diffusion at Scale: Introducing Mercury 3
sources.evidence: Later October 2026 announcement compares Mercury 3 size with Mercury 1 and context with Mercury 2.5. Mercury Edit 2 is not identified in the text, and no count or dense/MoE disclosure for it is established.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions - Inception Platform
sources.evidence: FAQ explicitly includes Mercury Edit 2 among models accepting text input only and says image generation is unsupported.

sources.title: Our Models - Inception
sources.evidence: Current opened page lists Mercury 3, Voice and Decide; its migration footnote concerns Mercury 2/2.5, not Edit 2. An older search-index excerpt mentions legacy Edit 2 support, so that excerpt is not treated as current access-policy evidence. API documentation and public model metadata remain available, but inference was not tested.

name.note: Exact product name in the developer announcement; API listing adds only the Inception display-name prefix.

developer.note: Released by Inception; service terms identify the company as Inception AI, Inc.

family.note: Mercury family label; this edit model is distinct from Mercury 2, 2.5, 3 and the older Coder variants.

release_date.note: Official index date plus immediate-availability announcement establish public release. The API created timestamp resolves to April 1, 2025 and is inconsistent with the explicit launch; do not substitute metadata creation or later provider-listing dates.

open_weights.note: Documented release is a proprietary hosted API/editor integration; no public checkpoint or open-weight grant is supplied in the first-party release, documentation or terms reviewed.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted model under Inception terms; not an asserted SPDX weight license.

parameters_b.note: No total parameter count for exact Mercury Edit 2 in the inspected launch, research index, original Mercury report or later model comparisons. Exact-name parameter/model-card/research searches did not locate a first-party disclosure. Later sibling size statements cannot determine this model count.

active_parameters_b.note: No exact-model active parameter count or routing disclosure found in the reviewed first-party sources. Do not equate active and total counts or transfer counts from Coder or chat siblings.

architecture.note: Exact-model launch explicitly describes diffusion and parallel token generation. The denoiser backbone and dense versus MoE status remain undisclosed for Edit 2. The 2025 Transformer disclosure describes Coder Mini/Small and is not exact-model evidence.

context_window.note: Unresolved first-party conflict: docs specify FIM 32K and NextEdit 32K with 8192 output, while both live exact-model listings return 128000 context and 32000 output. OpenAPI request schemas cap output at 8192, further conflicting with metadata. Clear baseline 32000 rather than choose a source without evidence of the actual accepted limit; no authenticated generation test was performed.

modalities.note: Live exact-model metadata states text input/output; FAQ independently confirms text-only input and no image generation.

reasoning.note: No dedicated reasoning mode in the documented API: exact model supports only FIM/edit, both exhaustive request schemas lack reasoning controls, supported_features is empty, and reasoning-effort documentation restricts controls to named chat models. This is an endpoint-mode assessment, not a claim that the model cannot solve reasoning tasks.

tool_call.note: Both supported endpoint descriptions explicitly prohibit tool calling; exact-model metadata exposes only these endpoints and no supported features.

description.value: Code editing dLLM for autocomplete (FIM) and next-edit suggestions
description.note: Accurate concise synthesis of the diffusion launch and the exact-model API description; avoids unsupported performance or backbone assertions.

patch.notes: Mercury Edit 2 is a diffusion code-editing model; its denoiser backbone, dense/MoE status and total/active parameter counts are undisclosed. Context is unresolved: the model documentation specifies 32K for FIM and NextEdit, but both public live model listings return 128,000 context and 32,000 output tokens; the documented request schemas limit output to 8,192. Public release is March 30, 2026, not the inconsistent April 1, 2025 metadata creation timestamp. No dedicated reasoning mode or tool calling is exposed on its documented FIM/edit endpoints. Current inference availability was not tested.

sources.label: Inception Blog: Mercury Edit 2 launch index

summary: Audited all 14 fields. Add proprietary license and diffusion architecture, with denoiser backbone and dense/MoE details left undisclosed. Total/active counts remain undisclosed after checking exact-model launch and later first-party comparisons/research. Clear context_window because live exact-model listings (128000) contradict documentation (32000); retain the explicit March 30, 2026 public release rather than stale API creation metadata. Text, FIM/next-edit description, no dedicated API reasoning mode, and no tool calling are confirmed.
